# New renderings, iliad-141 (22.289–404)

| Greek | `l` | `i` | avoided on purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| Δηΐφοβον … λευκάσπιδα (22.294) | "Deiphobus of the white shield" | "white-shielded Deiphobus" | "bright-shielded", "of the shining shield" (φαεινός is "shining"); λευκός "white" (Odyssey table), ἀσπίς "shield" |
| ᾔτεέ μιν δόρυ μακρόν (22.295) | "he was asking him for a long spear" | "asked him for a long spear" | "begged", "demanded"; αἰτέω "ask for" |
| ἀσπουδί … καὶ ἀκλειῶς (22.304) | "without a fight and without glory" | "without a fight and without glory" | "without trouble" (the table’s ἀσπουδί, 8.512, which fits a different context), "without a struggle" (avoided there); departure from 8.512, the sense follows the context and the note says so |
| ἀλλὰ μέγα ῥέξας τι καὶ ἐσσομένοισι πυθέσθαι (22.305) | "but having done something great, for those yet to come to hear of" | "after doing some great deed for men yet to come to hear of" | "to be learned of by", "for future generations"; ἐσσόμενοι "those yet to come" (11.76) |
| ἔγνω ᾗσιν ἐνὶ φρεσί (22.296) | "knew in his own wits" | "understood in his own mind" | "in his heart" (θυμός); φρένες "wits" in `l`, "mind" in `i`, as in the table |
| οἵ με πάρος γε πρόφρονες εἰρύατο (22.302–303) | "who before were ready-minded to guard me" | "who before this readily guarded me" | "protected", "kept me safe" (the table’s ἐρύομαι is "guarded", 4.186); πρόφρων "ready-minded" (Odyssey 14.406) |
| ἁρπάξων ἢ ἄρν’ ἀμαλὴν ἤ πτῶκα λαγωόν (22.310) | "to snatch either a tender lamb or a cowering hare" | "to snatch a tender lamb or a cowering hare" | "timid", "shy", "trembling"; πτώξ is "one that cowers" (πτώσσω) |
| ἐρεβεννῶν (νεφέων, 22.309) | "murky" | "murky" | "dark", "black" (kept for μέλας, κυάνεος); follows ἐρεβεννός "murky" (5.659) |
| τινάσσων φάσγανον ὀξύ (22.311) | "swinging his sharp sword" | "swinging his sharp sword" | "brandishing" (kept for ἀμπεπαλών), "shaking" (kept for σείω); τινάσσω "swing" |
| κόρυθι δ’ ἐπένευε φαεινῇ τετραφάλῳ (22.314–315) | "with his shining helmet he nodded, four-ridged" | "he nodded with his shining four-ridged helmet" | "bright", "gleaming"; φαεινός "shining", τετράφαλος "four-ridged" (12.384) |
| πάλλεν (δεξιτερῇ, 22.320) | "was shaking" | "shook" | "brandished" (kept for ἀμπεπαλών), "poised", "swung"; πάλλω "shake" (3.316) |
| εὐήκεος (αἰχμῆς, 22.319) | "well-pointed" | "well-pointed" | "keen", "sharp-edged"; matches ταναήκεϊ "long-pointed" |
| ἕσπερος … κάλλιστος … ἀστήρ (22.317–318) | "the evening star, the fairest star" | "the evening star, the fairest star" | "Hesperus" (a name the poet withholds), "brightest"; ἕσπερος "evening" (Od. 18.306) |
| ψυχῆς ὤκιστος ὄλεθρος (22.325) | "the destruction of life is swiftest" | "the destruction of life comes swiftest" | "soul" (ψυχή is "life" in the table’s θυμοῦ καὶ ψυχῆς, 11.334, and 9.423), "death" |
| λαυκανίην (22.325) | "the throat" | "the throat" | "gullet", "neck" (kept for αὐχήν) |
| μελίη … χαλκοβάρεια (22.328) | "the ash-spear, bronze-heavy" | "the bronze-weighted ash spear" | "bronze-bearing", "bronze-headed"; μελίη "ash", βαρύς "heavy" |
| ἀσφάραγον … τάμε (22.328) | "cut through the windpipe" | "sever the windpipe" | "gullet", "throat" (kept for λαυκανίη) |
| ὃ δ’ ἐπεύξατο δῖος Ἀχιλλεύς (22.330, whole-clause speech introduction) | "and he vaunted over him, heavenly Achilles:" | "heavenly Achilles cried out in triumph over him:" | "boasted", "said exultantly"; ἐπεύχομαι "vaunt" / "cry out in triumph" (table 13.373) |
| ἀτάρ που ἔφης (22.331) | "but you said, I suppose" | "you said, I suppose" | "no doubt you thought", "surely you imagined"; που "I suppose" |
| ἐξεναρίζων (22.331) · ἐξενάριξε (22.376, of a body already dead) | "despoiling" · "despoiled" | "stripping … of his armour" · "stripped … of his armour" | "killing", "slaying" (Hector is dead at 376; the table’s "killed … and stripped" at 5.151 is dropped to "stripped" there); ἐναρίζω "strip of armour" |
| ἀοσσητὴρ μέγ’ ἀμείνων (22.333) | "a far better helper" | "a far better helper" | "defender", "protector"; ἀοσσητήρ "helper" |
| ὅς τοι γούνατ’ ἔλυσα (22.335) | "I who loosened your knees" | "I, who have loosened your knees" | "who struck you down", "who unstrung your limbs"; λύω "loosen" |
| ἑλκήσουσ’ ἀϊκῶς (22.336) | "will drag about in unseemly fashion" | "will drag you about in unseemly fashion" | "tear", "maul", "shamefully"; ἀϊκῶς taken with ἀεικής "unseemly" (1.341) |
| τὸν δὲ κτεριοῦσιν Ἀχαιοί (22.336) | "but to him the Achaeans will render funeral rites" | "the Achaeans will pay him funeral honours" | "bury" (loses κτέρεα); follows the table’s κτεριοῦσι (11.455): `l` "render funeral rites", `i` "pay funeral honours" |
| λίσσομ’ ὑπὲρ ψυχῆς καὶ γούνων σῶν τε τοκήων (22.338) | "I beg you by your life and your knees and your parents" | "I beg you by your life, by your knees and by your parents" | "I implore", "I entreat" (kept for γουνάζομαι); λίσσομαι "beg" (1.394) |
| μή με ἔα … κύνας καταδάψαι (22.339) | "do not let the dogs devour me" | "do not let the dogs devour me" | "tear", "eat"; καταδάπτω "devour" |
| χαλκόν τε ἅλις χρυσόν τε δέδεξο (22.340) | "accept bronze in plenty and gold" | "accept bronze and gold in plenty" | "take", "receive"; δέχομαι "accept", ἅλις "in plenty" |
| μή με κύον γούνων γουνάζεο (22.345) | "Do not, dog, entreat me by my knees nor by my parents" | "Do not entreat me by my knees or my parents, dog" | "beg" (kept for λίσσομαι); γουνάζομαι "entreat" (table 1.427) |
| αἲ γάρ πως αὐτόν με μένος καὶ θυμὸς ἀνήη (22.346) | "would that my might and my heart would somehow urge me myself" | "If only my might and my heart would somehow drive me" | "rage", "fury" (μῆνις/χόλος words); μένος "might", θυμός "heart" (not "life", which is θυμός of the departing breath) |
| ὤμ’ ἀποταμνόμενον κρέα ἔδμεναι (22.347) | "to cut off your flesh and eat it raw" | "to cut off your flesh and eat it raw" | "carve", "devour"; ὠμός "raw" |
| ὡς οὐκ ἔσθ’ ὃς … ἀπαλάλκοι (22.348) | "so surely is there no one who could keep the dogs from your head" | "As surely as there is no one who can keep the dogs from your head" | "no one will", "there is no one who will save"; ἀπαλέξω "keep off" |
| εἰκοσινήριτα ἄποινα (22.349) | "ten times and twenty times over a ransom" | "ten and twenty times as much ransom" | "countless", "unstinted" (ἀπερείσια, 1.13); the sense of the second part of the compound is not known, and the note says so |
| στήσωσ’ ἐνθάδ’ ἄγοντες (22.350) | "set down here, bringing it" | "set down here, bringing it" | "weigh out", "pay"; ἵστημι "set" |
| ἐρύσασθαι (σε χρυσῷ, 22.351) | "redeem you with gold" | "buy you back with gold" | "rescue" (the Odyssey’s `l` for ἐρύσατο, 2.859), "ransom" (kept for ἄποινα); ἐρύομαι "draw back, redeem" |
| ἐνθεμένη λεχέεσσι γοήσεται (22.353) | "having laid you on the bier, lament you" | "lay you on the bier and lament you" | "bed" (λέχος is bed, "bier" here by context), "mourn", "bewail" (the table’s γοήσεται, 21.124, is "lament"); γοάω "lament" |
| κύνες τε καὶ οἰωνοὶ κατὰ πάντα δάσονται (22.354) | "the dogs and the birds will share you out in every part" | "the dogs and the birds will divide you up, every part of you" | "devour", "tear to pieces" (the verb is δαίομαι "divide"); the note says the sense |
| ἦ σ’ εὖ γιγνώσκων προτιόσσομαι (22.356) | "Truly I look at you and know you well" | "Truly I know you well as I look at you" | "foresee", "recognise"; προτιόσσομαι "look at" |
| σιδήρεος ἐν φρεσὶ θυμός (22.357) | "the heart in your wits is of iron" | "the heart in your mind is iron" | "a heart of iron in your breast" (φρένες are "wits", "mind", not "breast"; στῆθος is "chest"); σιδήρεος "of iron" (15.329) |
| μή τοί τι θεῶν μήνιμα γένωμαι (22.358) | "lest I become for you some cause of the gods’ wrath" | "that I do not become a cause of the gods’ wrath against you" | "a curse upon you", "the gods’ anger"; table’s θεῶν μήνιμα (11.73) "a cause of the gods’ wrath" |
| ἐσθλὸν ἐόντ’ (22.360) | "good as you are" | "good warrior that you are" | "brave" (the table keeps ἐσθλός "good" in both layers, 2.365), "noble"; ἐσθλός "good" of men in battle |
| ἀνουτητί (22.371) | "without wounding him" | "without wounding him" | "unscathed", "without a blow"; from οὐτάω "wound", with ἀ- privative |
| εἴπεσκε καὶ οὐτήσασκε παραστάς (22.375) | "would say, and would wound him, standing beside him" | "would speak, and standing beside him would wound him" | "stab", "strike"; οὐτάω "wound" (as at 22.371) |
| ἐξεναρίζων · ἐξενάριξε (see above) · στὰς ἐν Ἀχαιοῖσιν ἔπεα πτερόεντ’ ἀγόρευεν (22.377) | "standing among the Achaeans he spoke winged words" | "he stood among the Achaeans and spoke winged words" | "addressed"; table’s ἔπεα πτερόεντα "winged words" (ἀγορεύω "spoke") |
| ὅσ’ οὐ σύμπαντες οἱ ἄλλοι (22.380) | "as much as not all the others together" | "more evil than all the others together" | "than the whole army did"; the Greek is "as many as all the others together did not", and `i` says what it means |
| ἄκρην πόλιν (22.383) | "the high city" | "the city on its height" | "the citadel", "the acropolis" (a name for something the poet only describes); ἄκρος "high" |
| ἄκλαυτος ἄθαπτος (22.386) | "unwept, unburied" | "unwept and unburied" | "without mourning", "without a grave" |
| φίλα γούνατ’ ὀρώρῃ (22.388) | "my own knees move" | "my own knees move" | "my dear knees", "my knees stir"; φίλος as the possessive "own" (the table’s φίλος "own") |
| εἰ δὲ θανόντων περ καταλήθοντ’ εἰν Ἀΐδαο (22.389) | "if indeed they forget the dead in the house of Hades" | "if, in the house of Hades, they forget the dead" | "if the dead forget" (the Greek does not name the forgetters), "among the dead"; Ἀΐδαο "(house) of Hades" (22.213) |
| ἀείδοντες παιήονα (22.391) | "singing a paean" | "singing a paean" | "a song of victory", "a hymn"; παιήων is the song itself, and the note says what it is |
| ἠράμεθα μέγα κῦδος (22.393) | "We have won great glory" | "We have won great glory" | "carried off" (kept for οἴσεσθαι, 22.217), "earned"; ἄρνυμαι "win" |
| ᾧ Τρῶες κατὰ ἄστυ θεῷ ὣς εὐχετόωντο (22.394) | "to whom the Trojans through the town prayed as to a god" | "to whom the Trojans prayed, throughout the town, as to a god" | "boasted", "vowed"; εὐχετάομαι "pray"; ἄστυ "town" (2.801) |
| Ἕκτορα δῖον ἀεικέα μήδετο ἔργα (22.395) | "for heavenly Hector devised unseemly deeds" | "planned unseemly deeds against heavenly Hector" | "shameful deeds", "ugly deeds"; ἀεικής "unseemly" (1.341, 11.429), μήδομαι "devise" |
| βοέους δ’ ἐξῆπτεν ἱμάντας (22.397) | "attached oxhide straps" | "fastened oxhide straps through them" | "thongs" (the table’s ἱμάς is "strap", 8.544), "leather straps", "cords"; βόειος "of oxhide" (Odyssey 20.142) |
| κάρη δ’ ἕλκεσθαι ἔασεν (22.398) | "let the head drag" | "left the head to drag" | "let the head trail"; ἕλκω "drag" (as at 22.336) |
| μάστιξέν ῥ’ ἐλάαν, τὼ δ’ οὐκ ἀέκοντε πετέσθην (22.400) | "he lashed the horses to drive, and the two, not unwilling, flew" | "lashed the horses to drive; and the two flew on, not unwilling" | "eager", "willing"; ἀέκων "unwilling", the dual "the two" |
| κονίσαλος (22.401) | "a cloud of dust" | "a cloud of dust" | "a dust-cloud", "dust"; the table’s dust-cloud avoided at 16.374 |
| χαῖται κυάνεαι πίτναντο (22.401–402) | "dark hair streamed out" | "his dark hair spread out on either side" | "black", "blue" (κυάνεος is "dark", 1.528); πίτναμαι "spread out" |
| κάρη δ’ ἅπαν … πάρος χαρίεν (22.402–403) | "the head, all of it, … formerly graceful" | "the whole head, once so graceful" | "handsome", "lovely"; χαρίεις "graceful" |
| δῶκεν ἀεικίσσασθαι ἑῇ ἐν πατρίδι γαίῃ (22.404) | "gave to maltreat him in his own native land" | "gave it to his enemies to maltreat him in his own native land" | "dishonour", "outrage"; ἀεικίζω "maltreat" (from ἀεικής "unseemly"), ἑός "his own" |
